assumptions: Exactly two processes, at most one passage each.
Sequential consistency and individually atomic shared reads and writes.
Both processes use the same fixed flag-first or turn-first read order; both initial turn values are covered.
The theorem path reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
non_goals: No weak-memory or executable-code refinement claim.
summary: No finitely reachable state has both processes critical, for either initial turn and either fixed shared read order.
title: One-passage two-process mutual exclusion
verification_basis: Model-generated summary and proof; Erik Peterson directed the project and is holder of applicable rights. The pinned Lean development checked Peterson.peterson_mutual_exclusion. Kernel checking establishes the encoded proposition; source correspondence was reviewed separately.

assumptions: The one-passage two-process model and read-order assumptions from the safety record.
Continuously enabled participating protocol steps, including exit flag clearing, are weakly fair.
Every critical-section occupant eventually finishes critical work.
The theorem path reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
non_goals: No unconditional scheduling or critical-work termination guarantee.
summary: Every pending observation has some new process entry at that observation or later under protocol fairness and critical-work completion.

assumptions: Exactly two processes under the one-passage shared-memory semantics.
Restart is optional, private, and available only after the exit flag write.
Both fixed read orders and both initial turn values are covered.
The theorem path reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
non_goals: Safety requires no fairness and implies no request service.
No cancellation, crash, early restart, weak-memory, or executable-client claim.
summary: Mutual exclusion is preserved across any finite number of complete passages and optional private restarts.

assumptions: The repeated two-process model and request boundary in Peterson.Repeated.Specification.
Continuously enabled participating protocol steps, including exit, are weakly fair.
Every critical-section occupant eventually finishes critical work.
The theorem path reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
non_goals: No elapsed-time, total-step, or read bound.
No crash recovery, cancellation, weak-memory, or arbitrary client refinement.
summary: Every flag-write request eventually reaches its own serving entry when protocol steps are fair and critical work completes.

assumptions: Every finite process count n at least two is represented as m+2.
One passage per process under sequential consistency and individually atomic shared accesses.
Each level scans peers in ascending identifier order, one Q cell per transition, then reads TURN separately when needed.
Initial Q is zero and every initial TURN cell names source process 1.
The theorem paths report only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
non_goals: No n-process progress, repeated-use, or arbitrary scan-order theorem.
No snapshot, weak-memory, or executable-code claim.
summary: For every finite n at least two and 0 ≤ k ≤ n-1, at most n-k processes have passed level k without clearing Q; hence at most one process is critical.

assumptions: The repeated two-process model and flag-write request boundary.
Prefix bounds need validity only; bounded service additionally needs protocol fairness and critical completion.
Counts use peer entry events in open finite intervals.
Sharpness covers both read orders, both requester identities, and both initial turn values.
The theorem paths report only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
non_goals: No wall-clock, total-step, scheduling-delay, or read bound.
No arbitrary-n overtaking, weak-memory, or executable-client claim.
summary: From a request's flag write through service, zero peer entries occur before its turn write and at most one occurs overall; one is attainable for every reviewed order, actor and initial turn.
